The existing local fanout shares two aligned center phases, but a nonadjacent schedule cannot use the second result at its original cut without storing it. I narrowed to the exact zero-storage early-fanout mechanism and its first local falsifier before spending on a 144-call census.
bottleneck_link: If valid, the two-call local profile would change eight rank-8 center children and center charge 64 per call to four rank-8 children and charge 32 per call; the ideal complex ceiling multiplier is 1.90. The unchanged bit side limits a whole-bound gain to about 3.45%. Exact actual-profile overhead budgets: research/centre-sharing-overhead-budget/README.md, pinned as provenance in SOURCES.json.
stop_rule: For the exact common-frame scalar projection, one basis-channel endpoint mismatch is sufficient to terminate the no-storage early-fanout route. The pinned run finds mismatch in all eight channels (8/8 basis columns) and no persistent storage or full-phase-reordering alternative is tested. This finite result is not generalized beyond the stated projection.
